intent: To demonstrate that nuclear power generates a larger share of global electricity than solar energy.

units.meaning: Nuclear power accounts for 10.6% of global electricity generation.

basis.note: Printed percent value; mapped to nuclear by intent/narration.

accepted_routes: Nuclear's global electricity share is about 10.6%
10.6% of world electricity comes from nuclear
units.visual_evidence_rule: The segment labeled nuclear (or left) must be visible with its 10.6% value, or the value must appear in a label/callout.
units.temporal_anchor: When nuclear power's share is introduced.
units.reviewer_question: Is the explicit nuclear 10.6% value required, or can the video imply it from the larger segment?

units.meaning: Solar energy accounts for 6.3% of global electricity generation.

basis.note: Printed percent value; mapped to solar by intent/narration.

accepted_routes: Solar's global electricity share is around 6.3%
6.3% of world electricity comes from solar
units.visual_evidence_rule: The segment labeled solar (or right) must be visible with its 6.3% value, or the value must appear in a label/callout.
units.temporal_anchor: When solar energy's share is introduced.
units.reviewer_question: Is the explicit solar 6.3% value required, or can the video imply it from the smaller segment?

units.meaning: Nuclear power has a larger share of global electricity generation than solar energy.
accepted_routes: Nuclear's share is larger than solar's
Nuclear outranks solar by share, 10.6% vs 6.3%
Solar is lower than nuclear, 6.3% vs 10.6%
Nuclear leads solar in global electricity share
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both nuclear and solar values/labels must be visible together, or an explicit comparison annotation must show nuclear > solar.
units.temporal_anchor: During the while/comparison clause or final conclusion.
units.reviewer_question: Is the explicit nuclear > solar inequality required, or do the two separate values suffice?

units.meaning: Nuclear power's share exceeds solar energy's share by 4.3 percentage points.
accepted_routes: Nuclear is 4.3 percentage points higher than solar
The nuclear-solar gap is about 4.3 points, 10.6% vs 6.3%
Nuclear exceeds solar by roughly 4 percentage points
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both values must be visible and a difference annotation of 4.3 percentage points, or a clearly labeled gap, must appear.
units.temporal_anchor: During the comparison/conclusion if the gap is shown.
units.reviewer_question: Is the exact 4.3 percentage-point gap required, or optional elaboration?

optional_valid: Nuclear share is about 1.68 times solar share (10.6 / 6.3 = 1.68).
Solar share is about 59% of nuclear share (6.3 / 10.6 = 0.594).
Solar is the smaller of the two shares.
The two shares are not equal.
The combined nuclear and solar share is 16.9% (10.6 + 6.3) if using the same global electricity denominator.
unsupported_to_avoid: Nuclear supplies 10.6% of all global energy (wrong denominator; table is electricity generated).
Solar supplies 6.3% of total energy (wrong denominator).
Nuclear is 4.3% larger than solar (should be percentage points or a relative ratio, not percent).
Nuclear is the clear winner as an evaluative/causal claim beyond the numeric share comparison.
Nuclear share will increase or solar share will decline (extrapolation).
Nuclear causes more electricity than solar (causal; shares are not absolute generation).
notes: Left/right mapping to nuclear/solar comes from intent/narration; table entity labels are generic. Required set likely includes both share values and the nuclear>solar comparison; the 4.3-point gap and ratio are optional elaborations.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
